original_question: For each 1 <= p < infinity, determine the exact operator norm of the backward shift B on the Hardy space H^p(T), where B acts by Bf(e^{i theta}) = e^{-i theta}(f(e^{i theta}) - f_hat(0)).
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, Open problem 5.4, which restates a special case of Open problem 5.2 from Section 5.1: determining the exact norm of the backward shift on the classical Hardy spaces H^p.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper’s actual target: the classical backward shift on the classical Hardy space H^p(T), over the full range 1 ≤ p < ∞, and asks for its exact operator norm.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is an open problem, not a theorem: specifically Open problem 5.4 in Section 5.2.
The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the classical Hardy space H^p(T) of complex-valued functions on the unit circle T, viewed as a subspace of L^p(T).
To make the question stand-alone, H^p(T) should be defined by the Fourier condition f̂(n) = 0 for all n < 0.

The norm in question should be stated explicitly as the operator norm ||B||_{H^p(T)→H^p(T)} induced by the usual H^p-norm (equivalently the L^p(T)-norm on boundary values, with normalized Lebesgue measure).
The notation f̂(0) should be identified as the zeroth Fourier coefficient of f.
It is helpful to note the equivalent coefficient-shift description B(Σ_{n≥0} a_n e^{inθ}) = Σ_{n≥0} a_{n+1} e^{inθ}, which makes clear that B maps H^p(T) into itself.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should not be broadened to weighted Hardy spaces or abstract Hardy spaces; this open problem is posed only for the classical H^p case, even though the paper discusses broader spaces elsewhere.
The surrounding context in the paper notes that Open problem 5.4 is singled out as a particularly interesting special case of Open problem 5.2; that relation is implicit in the draft.
refined_question: For each real p with 1 ≤ p < ∞, let H^p(T) = {f ∈ L^p(T) : f̂(n) = 0 for all n < 0}, where T is the unit circle with normalized Lebesgue measure and f̂(n) denotes the nth Fourier coefficient. Define the backward shift B:H^p(T)→H^p(T) by (Bf)(e^{iθ}) = e^{-iθ}(f(e^{iθ}) − f̂(0)) (equivalently, if f(e^{iθ}) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n e^{inθ}, then Bf = Σ_{n≥0} a_{n+1} e^{inθ}). Determine the exact value of the operator norm ||B||_{H^p(T)→H^p(T)} as a function of p.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official target, but the exact item in the paper is Open problem 5.4 in Section 5.2, not any result from Section 1. The nearby context shows that this question is posed specifically for the classical Hardy spaces H^p and is highlighted as a special case of Open problem 5.2 from Section 5.1. The introduction supplies the paper’s Hardy-space notation via Fourier coefficients, so a faithful stand-alone rewrite should explicitly define H^p(T), specify the norm being used, and keep the scope strictly at the classical backward shift on H^p(T), without expanding to weighted or abstract Hardy spaces.
